items.title: Document Renamer
items.tagline: A desktop app that renames ebooks and documents by identifying their title, author, or journal metadata via the Claude API.
items.problem: A folder of ebooks or downloaded PDFs is often full of cryptic or inconsistent filenames, making them hard to browse or file away.
items.approach: Built a tkinter GUI that extracts leading text from each PDF/EPUB/DOCX/etc., sends it to the Claude API to identify title/author (Books) or author/year/keyword (Journals), and renames files into a consistent, configurable pattern. Includes an offline no-API-call fallback, OCR support for scanned PDFs, undo, and a dry-run preview.
items.outcome: A self-contained desktop app (Windows .exe and Linux .deb) that turns a folder of messy filenames into a consistently named, browsable library in one pass.
items.lessons: Batch-renaming tools live or die on trust — dry-run previews and a one-click undo matter as much as the identification logic itself.

items.title: DocSwap
items.tagline: A batch document converter GUI that converts between docx, rtf, txt, md, html, epub, latex, and pdf using pandoc.
items.problem: Converting documents between formats like docx, markdown, html, and pdf usually means juggling pandoc command-line flags one file at a time.
items.approach: Built a tkinter GUI on top of pandoc supporting batch conversion of files or whole folders, per-file output renaming, clickable results that open the converted file directly, and PDF export that prefers a LaTeX engine with a clearly flagged wkhtmltopdf fallback. Packaged as native installers for Debian/Ubuntu, Arch, and Fedora, with a Windows installer built from the same source.
items.outcome: A cross-platform desktop app that turns a folder of mixed-format documents into the target format in one batch, without touching the command line.
items.lessons: A thin GUI over a trusted CLI tool (pandoc) is mostly about batch ergonomics and clear dependency messaging (e.g. the PDF engine quality warning), not reimplementing the conversion logic itself.

items.title: GPG Encryptor
items.tagline: A point-and-click Tkinter GUI for encrypting and decrypting files and folders with GPG.
items.problem: Encrypting and decrypting files with GPG from the command line is error-prone for routine, repeated tasks like backups and one-off file sharing.
items.approach: Built a desktop GUI on top of GPG supporting recipient, password, and tar-password encryption modes, plus matching decrypt and tar-restore workflows, with dry-run previews and progress tracking. Packaged for one-command installation via pipx with a native desktop launcher.
items.outcome: A self-contained Linux desktop app installable with a single script, giving GPG encryption a proper GUI instead of remembering flag combinations.
items.lessons: Wrapping a well-understood CLI tool in a GUI is mostly about surfacing the right defaults and safety nets (dry runs, overwrite checks) rather than reinventing the underlying tool.

items.title: PDF to Markdown
items.tagline: A small command-line tool that converts a PDF file into a simple Markdown file.
items.problem: Converting a PDF's text into a clean, editable Markdown file usually means copy-pasting and manually fixing line breaks and bullets.
items.approach: Built a script on top of pdfplumber that extracts text page by page, normalises bullet-like lines into Markdown list syntax, and collapses stray blank lines. Packaged as a standalone Windows executable with PyInstaller and wrapped in an Inno Setup installer with an optional PATH entry.
items.outcome: A one-command converter that turns a PDF into a readable Markdown file, distributed as a Windows installer with no Python required on the target machine.
items.lessons: Even a small single-file script benefits from a proper installer (Start Menu entry, uninstaller, optional PATH) once it's meant to be shared beyond your own machine.

items.title: AD&D Character Generator
items.tagline: A character generator that follows the AD&D player book setup process.
items.problem: Manual AD&D character setup can be slow and repetitive, especially for new players who are still learning the process.
items.approach: Built a guided generator based on the AD&D player book flow, originally to make character creation easier and more engaging for my son.
items.outcome: A usable early version that mirrors core AD&D character creation steps while making the process faster and easier to follow.
items.lessons: Mapping tabletop rules into software works best when each step is explicit, validated, and easy to revisit.

items.title: Sams C++ 2005 Source Code
items.tagline: A student resource with extracted C++ examples organized by chapter.
items.problem: Working through a textbook is easier when code examples are available as separate files instead of embedded in long chapter text.
items.approach: Used a small extraction script to iterate through chapter material and split example code into individual .cpp files, organized by chapter for quick access.
items.outcome: A structured repository students can browse by chapter to find, compile, and experiment with the examples more easily.
items.lessons: Turning reference material into a learning resource often comes down to practical organization and fast lookup, not complex tooling.

items.title: Experimental Web Themes
items.tagline: CSS theme experiments exploring different visual directions and palette systems.
items.problem: Picking a single visual direction for a site is easier with working examples to compare instead of static mockups.
items.approach: Built a set of live theme demo pages that render the same home page layout against different color palettes defined in a shared themes dataset.
items.outcome: A gallery of interactive theme previews used to evaluate and settle on this site's visual direction.
items.lessons: Comparing full-page live renders side by side surfaces palette problems that swatches alone don't show.
